citation: Cote M et al. (authors per article) 'No evidence of pathogens associated with pulmonary MALT lymphoma using metagenomic next-generation sequencing', haematology/oncology journal, 2021
study_design: Retrospective case-series (frozen tissue biopsies analysed by mNGS); aetiological study of lymphoma, NOT a diagnostic-accuracy study

population.population_description: 13 patients with pulmonary MALT lymphoma plus 10 controls

index_test.platform_or_panel: agnostic metagenomic NGS, reads classified with Kaiju v1.4.1

reference_standard: Central histological review confirming MALT lymphoma; FISH for t(11;18)

diagnostic_yield.basis: No specific pathogen identified in the 13 MALT samples; A. xylosoxidans in 4/13 patients and 4/10 controls

quadas2_notes: Not a diagnostic-accuracy study of mNGS for infection in immunocompromised haemato-oncology patients; investigates microbial causes of lymphoma itself. Population not neutropenic/fever cohort.

evidence_quotes.claim: 13 pulmonary MALT lymphoma samples and 10 controls analysed by mNGS
evidence_quotes.quote: We included 13 samples from pulmonary MALT lymphoma (mean age: 60.3 years, 7 women, 3 with auto-immune background) and 10 controls.
No evidence of the presence of a specific pathogen was clearly identified in the group of patients with pulmonary MALT lymphoma.
We identified A. xylosoxidans sequence in 4/13 patients and in 4/10 controls.

The snap frozen large lung biopsies were analyzed by mNGS. After lung biopsies homogenization total nucleic acids (RNA and DNA) were extracted, amplified and classified according to their taxonomic assignment, after exclusion of host DNA.

exclusion_reason: Aetiological study of lymphoma pathogenesis, not diagnostic accuracy of mNGS for infections; small case-series (<5 relevant patients per group, no 2x2)
